Roles and nuances

  • Local Admin is an operational role mapped to an assigned zone or neighborhood; it is not an extra ancestry level and does not automatically equal Zone Admin. The master requires both Local and Zone portals; they share a scoped layout but distinct grants.
  • Country/Regional/City/Zone Admin can have narrower permissions than their scope. Being a City Admin does not automatically grant payout approval or raw identity-document export.
  • Dispatch Manager, KYC Reviewer, Finance Maker, Finance Checker, Support Agent, Security Analyst are additional staff roles, not public registration choices. Their scope remains constrained; finance maker cannot check the same action.
  • Vendor staff membership can be store-limited. Vendor owner cannot access a different legal vendor even if both operate in the same zone.
  • Rider access to recipient name/phone/address is limited to active assignment and a short post-delivery support window; no bulk customer export or browsing other offers' private data.
  • Customer may be both buyer and applicant/vendor/rider. Roles are additive but endpoints select the relevant capability; a vendor login does not grant admin access.
  • AI Agent has a unique workload identity, an allowed-tool list and the intersection of caller scope and agent scope. Read-only by default. Draft descriptions/answers/alerts are allowed where configured; money, permissions, KYC approval and ledger writes require the normal human command and cannot be executed through an AI shortcut.
  • Super Admin global access is audited and step-up protected. Direct DB maintenance uses separate privileged infrastructure access; no shared permanent human DB credential.

Mandatory negative tests

  1. Mymensingh City Admin requests Dhaka order, financial summary, export job, notification recipient list, KYC document and AI report: deny without leaking existence; no aggregate inclusion.
  2. Zone A Admin changes URL/body scope to Zone B or grants self Zone B: deny and audit.
  3. Vendor A requests Vendor B suborder by guessed ID; websocket subscribes to B; export includes B: deny/filter at backend and query layer.
  4. Rider A accepts Rider B offer, replays expired offer or accepts twice concurrently: at most one valid assignment.
  5. Customer A guesses B's order/tracking/recipient/KYC URL: deny; signed tracking token scoped and revocable.
  6. Staff with KYC review permission but no export permission attempts signed-URL or bulk export: deny.
  7. Revoked admin session calls API and reconnects socket after emergency lock: both denied; queued privileged jobs revalidate authority.
  8. AI asks tool to refund, approve KYC, edit ledger or change role: schema/policy denial; human approval endpoint still enforces maker–checker.
  9. Finance maker attempts checker approval or payout-destination change plus immediate payout: deny/cooldown.
  10. Lower-scope admin attempts global report cache key or search index query: scope required before cache/index access.

These are planned tests, not results. Permission changes bump authorizationVersion; all caches, sessions and socket rooms must observe revocation.

DESIGN DOCUMENT · 04-geographic-model.md

Geographic hierarchy, serviceability and remote ordering

Canonical hierarchy

Global (virtual root; not a tenant database)
└── Country (BD initially enabled; US prepared but disabled)
    └── Region / Division / State
        └── District
            └── City OR Upazila (country-configurable operational unit)
                └── Service Zone (business polygon, not necessarily a ward)
                    └── Neighborhood / Ward / Locality (optional)

Administrative boundary and service coverage are distinct. A city may launch only a few zones. Store service areas can span multiple zones only with authorization. A vendor is a legal business; Store is a pickup branch. This avoids losing the historical multi-city/branch requirement while preserving one vendor ledger.

Purbadhala is an upazila in Netrokona District, Mymensingh Division; it is not a child of Mymensingh City. Bangladesh Post's directory lists Purbadhala under Netrokona. 2 Proposed pilots are separate: Mymensingh City operational zones and Purbadhala operational zones. Exact polygons, launch status and participating stores require owner/operations approval. Voice transcripts contain spelling variants; no unsupported boundary is inferred from them.

Storage and polygon rules

  • PostgreSQL/PostGIS geometry SRID 4326 for input/exchange; validate latitude/longitude ranges and geometry validity. Use a suitable geography cast or projected geometry only for explicitly tested distance operations.
  • BoundaryVersion is append-only after approval; active pointer changes atomically. Store source, effective date, hash, approver and version. Keep the version used by each checkout/dispatch decision.
  • MultiPolygon supports enclaves; reject self-intersections and empty geometry. GiST indexes support point-in-polygon and candidate searches.
  • A zone must belong to exactly one City; ancestry must match Country→Region→District→City. A point in a parent boundary does not automatically mean service available.
  • Define overlap policy before launch: reject ambiguous overlapping active zones or resolve by explicit priority with a deterministic tie rule. Do not select the first SQL row.
  • Boundary points exactly on an edge use a documented PostGIS covers/contains policy and fixtures; no floating-point UI decision.
  • Map drawing is an admin proposal. Higher approval activates a version. Ordinary admins cannot change their own scope by editing a service polygon.
  • PostGIS access is implemented through typed repository adapters and reviewed SQL or a version-pinned supported ORM extension. Prisma's current PostGIS capabilities must be checked at implementation lock time; do not assume all spatial operators are native. 1 3

Recipient-first checkout

Buyer (any location within an enabled origin country)
  + Recipient (separate name/phone/address snapshot)
  → destination Country must equal enabled order country
  → destination City/Zone active and within operating hours
  → validated destination point + polygon version
  → eligible store service areas + sellable inventory
  → road route / delivery quote / fee / ETA
  → risk evaluation (buyer signals are not destination proof)
  → destination-scoped parent order + vendor suborders
  → destination-eligible rider dispatch

Deliver to Myself reuses a saved buyer address but still creates a recipient snapshot. Deliver to Someone Else collects the recipient independently. A Dhaka buyer can order for a Mymensingh recipient if that destination is supported. A buyer outside the destination zone is not fraud by that fact alone. Buyer GPS may be unavailable/declined; offer address-based checkout with risk-appropriate phone verification. Do not require buyer GPS to match recipient address.

The older conversation's strict buyer-GPS rule is explicitly superseded by master §10 and the later remote-ordering discussion. GPS, IP/VPN and device integrity are probabilistic risk inputs, never authoritative proof of recipient location. Phone OTP proves control of a number, not physical presence. No covert microphone/call access.

Access scope for cross-area records

Resource Scope anchor Important rule
Customer profile Consent + support purpose; country/zone only for assigned support Buyer residence does not grant buyer's city access to destination financial records
Vendor/store/product Store location and approved service areas Vendor owner limited to own business; admin scope intersects store/operational area
Parent order Recipient destination zone for local operations Buyer can always access own order; buyer-city admin does not automatically see remote destination order
Vendor suborder Destination zone + vendor/store City finance sees authorized destination operations, not other-city vendor ledger
Delivery/rider assignment Pickup + destination zones and rider grant Cross-zone job needs both service permissions or approved exception
Rider profile Home/assigned operational scope Relocating GPS does not rewrite admin assignment
Payment/refund/settlement Merchant country + explicit financial-scope anchor A zone operational role does not automatically receive bank data
Report/export/search/AI Same predicate as underlying rows Apply scope before aggregation/cache, not after

For a multi-zone or multi-store parent, return only authorized suborders to local staff; mask totals that would reveal other scopes. Country-level consolidation is available only to roles with all contributing scopes. Define financial reporting anchor explicitly before Phase 7; no accidental “buyer city gets all revenue” rule.

Rider eligibility and exceptions

Default own-zone work; time-limited neighboring-zone permission may be granted by an authorized higher admin. Every offer checks active KYC, vehicle class, active shift, consent, online status, capacity, allowed pickup/destination zones, location freshness/accuracy and road distance. Reject stale/spoof-suspect locations for new offers with a verification path. Do not cancel an existing delivery just because a rider crosses a boundary. Manual dispatch and temporary overrides require reason, expiry, actor and audit; they never bypass identity/KYC or create a second final assignment.

Google Routes exposes road distanceMeters, duration and traffic-aware routing options; Route Matrix supports multiple origins/destinations. Use these for route evidence, not an invented traffic payment multiplier. 1 2

Geographic acceptance fixtures (planned)

  • Same-country Dhaka→Mymensingh supported remote order succeeds without matching buyer GPS.
  • Unsupported/inactive destination, ambiguous polygon, cross-border destination and closed operating window fail clearly before payment capture.
  • Boundary revision does not rewrite historical order/fee evidence.
  • Purbadhala admin cannot read Mymensingh City or Dhaka records; Mymensingh regional admin can read only descendant scope.
  • Rider location stale, outside approved zone, expired override or inactive KYC prevents new offer; active delivery gets safe exception handling.
  • SQL, API, export, report, cache and websocket tests all enforce the same scope.
DESIGN DOCUMENT · 05-security-threat-model.md

Security threat model and verification plan

Status: proposed controls; none claimed implemented or penetration-tested. Review date: 2026-11-01.

Assets and trust boundaries

Assets: identity credentials/TOTP/recovery codes, privileged sessions, NID/passport/trade/driving documents, bank/MFS destinations, buyer/recipient PII, rider live location, order/inventory integrity, provider credentials, immutable journals, payout instructions, audit evidence, consent/preferences and backup keys.

Boundaries: browser→BFF; BFF→API; identity redirect; API→DB/Redis/object store; provider callbacks; admin→KYC; worker→payment/payout; AI→tools; export→download; logs/telemetry; public CDN→private storage. A frontend role label, uploaded document, GPS coordinate, payment screenshot, QR scan or AI output is never proof of authorization/payment/identity by itself.

Threat register

ID / priority Threat and attack path Required prevention/detection Acceptance evidence
T01 Critical Vendor/customer/admin IDOR via guessed IDs, search, export or socket room Server RBAC + ownership + geographic ABAC; scoped repository/RLS; field projection; room authorization Cross-tenant/cross-city API, socket, export and aggregate tests
T02 Critical Admin credential theft or public admin registration Invitation/provisioning only; verified identity; mandatory TOTP; new-device challenge; risk evaluation; session/device revocation Admin cannot reach dashboard with password only; enrollment/recovery/revocation tests
T03 Critical OAuth account takeover by matching unverified email or altered callback OIDC code+PKCE, state/nonce, exact redirect allowlist, issuer/subject identity; no automatic email-only merge; proof-based linking Forged state, wrong issuer, duplicate email and unverified provider-email tests
T04 Critical Duplicate order/assignment/earning/payout under retries or concurrency DB transactions, unique business keys, row locks, version checks, balanced append-only journals, outbox/inbox Parallel requests and worker replay produce one financial effect
T05 Critical Fake provider callback, replay, amount/currency substitution or success-page spoof Provider-specific authenticity verification + server transaction query; exact merchant/order/amount/currency; unique event key Tampered/replayed/out-of-order callbacks never mark paid twice
T06 Critical Payout destination substitution / insider transfer fraud Verified ownership, masked details, step-up, change cooldown, maker–checker, destination snapshot, provider idempotency Same maker/checker rejected; changed destination holds payout
T07 Critical KYC document leak via public bucket, long-lived URL, logs or other reviewer Private encrypted quarantine/active buckets, short-lived signed access, no indexing, scoped reviewer assignment, read audit, retention job Unauthorized direct/signed URL and cross-scope reviewer tests; expiry/scanning evidence
T08 High SQL injection / unsafe raw PostGIS query / RLS context leakage in pool Parameterized SQL, allowlisted sort/filter, least-privileged runtime, SET LOCAL context, no BYPASSRLS Injection fixtures and pooled concurrent-scope tests
T09 High XSS/CSRF/clickjacking on admin or storefront Contextual escaping, sanitization, CSP nonce, no dangerous HTML, Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite cookies, origin checks + CSRF tokens, frame policy Script payload and cross-origin mutation tests; security-header scan
T10 High Upload malware, SVG script, decompression bomb, content-type spoof Size/page/dimension limits, magic-byte validation, reject active formats, antivirus quarantine, image re-encode, metadata stripping Malformed/oversized/mislabelled files rejected before review
T11 High Refresh/session replay, fixation, stale permissions Opaque high-entropy token hashed at rest; rotate on login/privilege change; provider refresh rotation; authorization version; idle/absolute expiry Stolen old token and revoked-session API/socket rejection
T12 High TOTP brute force/replay/reset abuse Encrypted provider secrets, rate limits, short time window, consumed-step protection, single-use hashed recovery codes, step-up for reset Replayed code and repeated failure lockout tests; no secret in logs
T13 High COD deposit falsification, double allocation or deleting weekly debt Separate custody ledger; verified office/bank/merchant MFS evidence; allocation caps; immutable reversal; reconciliation Unverified screenshot never reduces due; duplicate deposit rejected
T14 High Rate/commission tampering or retrospective repricing Server-only effective versions, scope precedence, snapshots, future edits, overlap checks, approval/audit Boundary distances/time zones and historical-rate invariance tests
T15 High Fake order/coupon/bot/OTP abuse Risk rules, velocity controls, verified phone where needed, CAPTCHA adaptively, stock/coupon limits, manual review/appeal VPN-only signal holds/verifies rather than blanket rejection; confirmed fraud evidence required
T16 High Buyer/recipient GPS confusion and location spoofing Recipient address authoritative for service; separate buyer risk; accuracy/freshness checks; no perfect VPN/GPS claim Remote-order positive test and mocked/stale location risk test
T17 High Live rider location exposed after shift or to unrelated customer Consent + active shift/delivery gate, assignment-scoped room/token, expiry, stop tracking on end, short raw retention Offline rider cannot upload; unrelated/old token cannot subscribe
T18 Critical AI prompt injection causes payout, KYC approval or data exfiltration Separate agent identity; caller∩agent scope; read-only allowlist; untrusted retrieval content; no sensitive tools; exact-action human approval Injected instructions cannot call prohibited tool or widen report scope
T19 High Personalization becomes covert surveillance First-party consent only; no call/microphone/other-app collection; explicit voice/search/share; view/clear/opt-out/sync controls Denied consent stops events; deletion propagates to profiles/caches
T20 High Bulk insider export or screenshot leakage Data minimization/masking, export permission+approval, watermark/session trace, clipboard restrictions on sensitive fields, native controls where supported Export audit/approval; watermark verified; documented browser limitations
T21 Critical Compromised admin persists after incident Emergency Security Lock revokes privileged sessions/tokens/rooms, pauses privileged jobs, bumps auth version, alerts security Revocation propagation test and break-glass recovery drill
T22 High Dependency/CI/secret compromise Exact pins+lockfile, scan/SBOM, protected CI identity, secret manager, reviewed infra changes, artifact signing, least privilege No frontend secrets; dependency and IaC gates enforced
T23 High Backup loss, ransomware, destructive migration Encrypted immutable/offline copies, separate backup credentials, PITR, migration backup gate, restore drills, ledger reconciliation Documented measured RPO/RTO and restore integrity report
T24 High Country/feature flag accidentally enables cross-border/live payments Default false, environment separation, capability+legal gates, two-person activation, audit BD-only checkout; US/cross-border/live provider negative tests
T25 Medium Enumeration, scraping, business intelligence leak Generic auth/recovery responses, rate limits, pagination, bot protection, public/private DTO split, scoped totals No account-existence or hidden-scope count leakage

Authentication and sessions

Proposed browser flow: same-origin BFF → identity Authorization Code + PKCE → validated callback → encrypted server token envelope → opaque session cookie. API resolves session and current authorization on every request. Cookie: __Host- prefix where appropriate, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, no Domain; explicit CSRF/Origin protection for mutations. No tokens in localStorage, URLs, analytics or error reports.

Admin: password + Google Authenticator-compatible TOTP every login; initial QR enrollment and initial code verification; recovery codes shown once; new/suspicious device email challenge; session risk evaluation; KYC/provisioning approval before access. Historical “Gmail every login” is implemented as risk-based email challenge per final master, not sending a code to every login regardless of risk. Sensitive operations require recent TOTP step-up bound to exact action. Customer MFA optional; ordinary customer shopping does not require NID KYC.

Argon2id parameters must be explicitly configured and benchmarked, not accepted blindly from an identity-provider default. Start with a tested memory-hard profile around 64 MiB, tuned to infrastructure; record final parameters and login latency. Use a breached-password check where lawful, generic errors, per-account/IP limits and a recovery flow that does not bypass MFA. Identity provider owns secrets; application stores references/assurance, never plaintext passwords or TOTP seeds.

Proposed privileged idle timeout 15 minutes, absolute 8 hours; customer idle 7 days/absolute 30 days, configurable after risk review. These are policy proposals, not existing settings. Session/device list, login history, security notifications and revocation are required. Emergency lock must invalidate API and socket access even if an identity refresh token remains temporarily usable.

Authorization and database defense

Use deny-by-default RBAC plus geographic ABAC and owner checks. RLS policies cover core scoped tables; runtime role cannot bypass. Transaction-local verified context avoids pooled-session leakage. Security-definer routines, if any, require review and fixed search paths. Foreign keys and composite constraints prevent mismatched vendor/store/order/zone references. Do not rely on Prisma middleware alone. Audit logs and financial ledgers deny runtime UPDATE/DELETE; migration/deployment roles are separate.

Data protection and privacy

TLS everywhere; KMS envelope encryption for documents, payout details, identity-phone fields and provider credentials; key access separated from object access and audited. Product images may use CDN; KYC never. Signed KYC access proposed TTL 60 seconds, one object/reviewer/purpose, no-store and referrer protection; URL issuance itself audited. Download proxy may be preferable to a reusable signed URL.

Collect only policy-required documents. Vendor company/individual and rider bicycle/motorvehicle requirements differ. Retention periods require Bangladesh counsel/provider review before real collection; do not assert that a historical chat's cited “2026 privacy law” is verified. Lawful financial-record holds override deletion only for required records; explain exceptions. Proposed raw rider-location retention ≤30 days and personalization events ≤180 days are review targets, not legal advice. Minimize telemetry and redact recipient/KYC data.

Office-assisted uploads record subject consent, uploader, reviewer and source. No biometric templates by default. Government verification only through explicit authorized channels; public portals are not assumed APIs. Never scrape NID data. Manual review is labelled manual, not “government verified.”

Screenshot/recording limitation

A website cannot universally prevent OS screenshots, screen recording, developer tools access or another camera. Disabling right-click is not data security. Use visible dynamic watermarks (admin ID, session reference, scope, time), minimize/mask data, approve exports, audit reads and revoke sessions. Native Android FLAG_SECURE and supported iOS capture detection/masking apply only if a native wrapper is later approved. Do not claim invisible watermarks reliably identify every photograph or that audio recording can be blocked by CSS/JavaScript.

Payments, fraud and AI

Payment adapter must declare authentication method and capabilities. Signed webhook where offered; if a provider uses hash/IPN plus validation rather than a signed event, implement its documented verification and server query—never label an unsigned callback “signed.” SSLCOMMERZ's public v4 docs require transaction/amount/currency validation through its Order Validation API. 2 aamarPay recommends transaction search from the success endpoint. 3 Provider-specific contracts still control marketplace settlement.

AI can summarize, draft, recommend, answer scoped status and create low-risk alerts. It cannot transfer money, approve refunds/payouts/KYC, mutate ledger or grant roles. Human approval uses normal domain authorization and an exact payload hash; “AI suggested it” is never authority. Retrieval content is untrusted, tool results minimized, and all calls/denials logged. No access to private communications; user-initiated voice search and explicit product-link sharing are the allowed alternatives.

Release gates

No production launch until: negative permission tests, admin MFA/recovery/lock drills, KYC access/retention tests, concurrency/ledger/payout tests, provider callback/reconciliation tests, dependency/secret scans, upload tests, independent security review, backup restore drill, monitoring/alert drill and documented risk acceptance. WAF/TLS/CSP are controls, not a guarantee against compromise. Paid tooling and external penetration testing require owner approval.

DESIGN DOCUMENT · 06-finance-and-delivery-policy.md

Finance, COD, rider earnings and delivery policy

Status: design proposal with explicit approval points. No financial operation has been executed. Historical rates and screenshot amounts are examples only.

1. Money representation and source of truth

Use PostgreSQL BIGINT minor units and ISO currency per journal (BDT poisha initially); never binary floating point. Define rounding once per line and allocate discounts/tax deterministically so line sums equal parent totals. Percentages use basis points. A UI wallet is a projection of immutable ledger accounts, not an editable balance field.

Every journal balances debits and credits per currency. Runtime DB permissions deny ledger UPDATE/DELETE; corrections are linked reversals. Unique business-event keys prevent duplicate completion earnings, verified deposits, refunds and payout reservations. Balance snapshots are rebuildable and reconciled. Separate accounts/purposes:

  • Vendor gross receivable, commission, refund/adjustment, pending and completed settlement.
  • Rider delivery earnings, approved deductions, payout reserve and paid payout.
  • Rider COD custody/amount due, verified COD deposit clearing and allocations.
  • Gateway/QR/bank/cash clearing, platform delivery revenue, promotion subsidy, tax and payment fees.

Cash collected from a recipient is not rider income. A screenshot or rider-entered “deposit successful” is not a verified company receipt. A payout instruction is not proof of successful transfer until the approved provider/bank evidence confirms it.

2. Quote, commission and settlement

Customer quote: product subtotal − eligible discounts + delivery fee + applicable tax/transparent charges = total. Multiple vendor/store groups have independently allocated totals. Delivery price to the customer and rider compensation are separate policies; a free-delivery campaign does not imply a zero-cost rider.

Commission rule dimensions: country, city, zone, vendor, category and order type; percentage or fixed amount. Proposed precedence: explicit vendor/category combination → vendor → category/zone → category/city → category/country → zone/city/country default. Exact precedence must be approved and stored as a policy version; ambiguous equal-priority rules are rejected. Default basis is discounted product subtotal excluding delivery and tax unless a future approved rule says otherwise.

Commission becomes earned according to the configured successful-order policy, proposed at delivery completion; cancellation before completion does not create normal commission. Partial cancellation/refund uses a snapshot and an explicit proration/reversal policy. No retrospective recalculation when a rule changes.

Vendor net payable = eligible gross product sales − earned commission − refunds − approved adjustments, with delivery/tax liabilities tracked separately. Settlement eligibility requires verified payout destination, financial checks and configured return/hold policy. Historical COD discussion proposed waiting for verified company deposit: adopt as a conservative configurable gate, subject to owner approval. Settlement days for vendors remain configurable; no invented final Wednesday/Saturday schedule. Initial maker–checker manual settlement, later approved provider automation. Direct vendor acquiring/QR settlement must be reconciled, not paid a second time from the platform ledger.

3. Rider fixed-distance pay

Super Admin configures country/city/zone rule versions, effective dates, active status, distance slabs, minimum, optional maximum and routing method. Slabs use integer meters, lower-inclusive and upper-exclusive: [0,2000), [2000,4000), [4000,6000). Exactly 2,000m belongs to the second slab. Validate no gaps/overlaps; out-of-range distance escalates rather than silently inventing a rate. Optional maximum is a cap, not a hidden deduction.

Distance basis: verified pickup store → recipient destination road route, using configured vehicle/routing method. Rider → store road distance is used for dispatch ranking only. Do not pay extra for the rider's unrelated travel, traffic or waiting time. Traffic-aware ETA is allowed; it does not change fixed slab compensation. Historical suggestions of ৳30/45/60 and time-based bonuses are not approved rates; final master explicitly rejects the latter.

Snapshot point: final rider acceptance creates the assignment and immutable rate/route snapshot atomically (proposed default). If business chooses offer time instead, record that policy before implementation. Route recalculation for navigation does not rewrite earnings. A materially wrong pickup/destination or reassignment requires an audited exception/new delivery attempt and reversal where appropriate, never silent historical edits.

Normal earning credit occurs only after successful delivery completion, recipient verification and required COD accounting. Failed/refused delivery has no normal earning; any separately approved cancellation compensation would be a distinct policy/journal, not an automatic distance credit.

4. Atomic dispatch and delivery invariants

  1. Vendor manually confirms ready; preparation timer cannot do it.
  2. Create dispatch run; shortlist active, KYC-approved, consented, online, in-zone riders with fresh accurate location and available capacity.
  3. Use PostGIS for candidate filtering, then provider road-route matrix for ordering. Stable tie-breaker: configured priority → road distance → oldest offer fairness → rider ID. No straight-line fallback when road distance is required.
  4. Lock dispatch row; ensure no unexpired offer; create one 30-second offer using DB time. Commit, then emit socket/push hint.
  5. Acceptance locks offer, delivery and rider; checks token, status, expiry, current eligibility/capacity. Reject/timeout closes offer; create one active assignment on success.
  6. Delayed jobs are only wakes: database expiry/status decides. A BullMQ retry or duplicated socket cannot create a second assignment.
  7. Exhaustion goes to local dispatch queue/manual fallback. Manual assignment obeys the same KYC/zone/capacity checks and requires reason/audit. Temporary neighboring-zone grants expire.
  8. Pickup confirmation and recipient OTP are separate events. OTP is hashed/peppered, short-lived, rate-limited, attempt-limited and never logged or exposed to unrelated users. An authorized proof-of-delivery exception is distinct and reviewed.

One active delivery per rider initially; batching is a future explicitly approved feature. A rider going out of zone stops new offers and raises an alert, but does not automatically cancel an already assigned delivery. End shift stops new offers; active delivery completes or transfers safely.

5. Rider balance explanation

Display separately:

Completed delivery earnings (period / lifetime)
Approved deductions (itemized)
Payout reserve / pending payout
Paid payout
COD cash collected
Verified COD deposits
COD still due to company
Withdrawable earnings
Next scheduled payout and destination status

Proposed withdrawable = posted eligible earnings − approved earning deductions − reserved/in-flight/paid amounts − explicitly authorized COD offset reserve. COD due remains separately visible even when an approved offset applies. Never silently net all COD from earnings or describe COD custody as spendable balance. Automatic COD offset requires an approved, disclosed policy and a balanced transfer journal; otherwise collect deposits independently.

6. Sunday payout

  • Schedule: every Sunday in the country's operational timezone; BD Asia/Dhaka. Proposed weekly earning cutoff and Sunday processing hour are pending business approval; store exact UTC instant and local period label.
  • Default preference: automatic payout enabled, but eligibility blocked until a supported verified MFS/bank destination exists. No bank details means no bank payout; do not fabricate one.
  • Separate manual withdrawal request and bank-account option. Manual request uses the same destination, risk, balance and COD checks; Sunday-only vs additional manual window is a policy decision, with the final master's Sunday default retained.
  • Unique schedule key per rider/period/destination policy; reserve balance before network call. Retry the same provider idempotency key. Unknown result stays reserved and reconciles; never create a fresh payout just because a timeout occurred.
  • Successful payout transfers reserve to paid/cash clearing; failure releases reserve through a linked compensating journal. Paid payout cannot be “unpaid” by deleting a row.
  • Weekly counters may reset their display period, but transaction history and cumulative ledger never reset/delete. Show calculation, adjustment, fee, tax and provider reference for every payout.
  • Holiday/provider outage policy must be approved: next business day vs same Sunday attempt; record actual schedule reason. No claim of instant payout where the rail does not support it.

7. COD reconciliation

Supported submission channels: company-office cash, bank deposit, approved merchant MFS deposit. Personal rider/vendor accounts are not company settlement destinations. Record collection/receipt, expected amount, discrepancy, depositor, channel, merchant account reference, evidence and reviewer.

Office cash uses maker–checker where practical; bank/MFS deposit requires trusted statement/provider reconciliation, not an uploaded screenshot alone. Pending evidence does not reduce COD due. Verified deposit posts once and allocations cannot exceed deposit or outstanding collection amounts. Partial deposits, overpayments, duplicate references, reversals and unmatched deposits have explicit review queues. Daily reconciliation compares collection → custody → deposit → allocation → vendor settlement eligibility.

8. Worked example — TEST ONLY, not rates

Assume product subtotal BDT 1000.00, customer delivery fee 50.00, no tax/discount, approved commission 10%, approved rider slab pay 60.00. Customer total is 1050.00. Vendor product payable before other adjustments is 900.00; platform product commission is 100.00. Delivery revenue is 50.00 and rider delivery expense is 60.00: delivery margin is −10.00 before other costs. This shows why customer delivery fee and rider earnings must not be conflated. For COD, rider custody is 1050.00 until verified deposit; earning is 60.00, not 1110.00. For prepaid, COD custody is zero. Real tax, fees, refunds and subsidy funding require their own lines.

9. Historical subscriptions and loyalty (retained, not dropped)

Vendor plans: configurable Free/Basic/Plus/Pro, monthly prices, volume/unit limits, featured-listing/support entitlements, upgrade/downgrade, expiry, payment/subscription history. First-year free introductory access was requested; activation date, eligibility, what “free” includes (subscription vs commission/payment fees), renewal notice and post-trial consent need approval. Never silently charge after a trial. Historical 500/1000/1500 fees and 5000/10000 units are examples only.

Loyalty/cashback/referrals/membership were accepted in the historical conversation. Keep feature-flagged after core finance: append-only award/expiry/reversal events, financial liability for redeemable value, anti-self-referral, qualifying-order rules, budget limits and clear terms. AI may recommend campaigns, not issue unrestricted money.

10. Acceptance tests (planned)

  • Two identical checkout/payment/completion/deposit/payout commands produce one effect.
  • Concurrent rider acceptance yields one active assignment; expired offers fail even if socket arrives late.
  • Slab boundary, currency rounding, rate effective-time/timezone, min/max and historical invariance pass.
  • Every journal balances; attempted ledger edit/delete fails; reversal restores reconstructable balances.
  • COD due and rider earnings remain distinct; partial/unverified/duplicate deposits reconcile correctly.
  • Sunday scheduler uses Asia/Dhaka, verified destination, reserve and idempotent retry; missing bank/MFS blocks payout.
  • Vendor commission excludes delivery by default; partial refunds and multi-vendor allocation sum exactly.
  • Free-delivery subsidy is funded explicitly; subscription trial does not secretly waive or charge other fees.
  • Provider outage/unknown result never triggers duplicate money transfer or invented success.
DESIGN DOCUMENT · 07-kyc-workflow.md

KYC, privileged enrollment and verification workflow

Status: proposed policy. No identity documents have been collected; no government verification is connected.

Common lifecycle

DRAFT → SUBMITTED → SCAN_PENDING → UNDER_REVIEW → MORE_INFORMATION / APPROVED / REJECTED; later EXPIRING → RESTRICTED → RENEWAL_REVIEW. Account suspension is a separate status. Document status and overall case status are separate; one approved passport does not approve an entire company.

  1. Authenticated applicant selects role and country; server issues the exact required/conditional checklist from a versioned policy.
  2. Applicant gives consent; direct upload goes to private quarantine through an authorized short-lived upload session. An authorized office may assist upload, recording subject consent and uploader.
  3. Validate MIME/magic bytes, size/pages/dimensions, malware and document completeness; strip unnecessary metadata and encrypt. Store checksum, issuer, expiry, classification and restricted object key.
  4. Assign a scoped reviewer. Reviewer sees minimum data, masked identifiers by default and a short-lived download; every view/export is audited.
  5. Record per-document decision, reasons, evidence and method: MANUAL_DOCUMENT_REVIEW, AUTHORIZED_PROVIDER, AUTHORIZED_OFFICIAL_CHANNEL or IN_PERSON. Never claim official database verification without actual evidence.
  6. Approve the case only when all required checks pass. Applicant cannot approve self; reviewer/uploader separation is enforced where practical. High-risk staff/finance grants use maker–checker.
  7. Emit status event, notify applicant, revalidate eligibility at selling/shift-start/offer-acceptance/privileged access. Approval is not a permanent bypass.
  8. Expiry reminders (proposed 30/14/7 days, configurable), renewal grace only where policy permits, restrict new selling/delivery/privileged work when mandatory evidence expires. Existing deliveries finish safely; financial history remains.
  9. Rejection/resubmission preserves prior versions. Retention/deletion follows an approved schedule with legal-hold exceptions and storage/cache cleanup.

Vendor checklist

Category Individual / sole proprietor Company / authorized representative
Identity NID or passport where permitted; contact verification Representative NID/passport; authorization letter/board resolution
Business Valid trade license where applicable; business address Incorporation/registration and trade license as applicable; registered address
Tax TIN/BIN/VAT only where legally applicable Company TIN/BIN/VAT as applicable; do not demand nonexistent documents
Store Pickup address, store photos, operating hours Each branch address, pickup contact and photos
Financial Verified owner/business MFS/bank destination Verified company destination; beneficiary must match approved policy
Regulated goods Category-specific permits before publication Same; legal review before enabling category

Passport is not mandatory for every vendor when an accepted NID path exists. Business type controls documents. Commission/subscription settings do not replace KYC.

Rider checklist

Identity (NID/passport as permitted), phone/contact, address, emergency contact with appropriate consent, profile photo if required, vehicle type. Bicycle: no motor driving license/registration demand. Motorbike/car: applicable driving license, registration, fitness/tax token/insurance where required. Vehicle ownership or authorization evidence where policy requires. Verify payout destination separately. Rider cannot accept offers while pending/rejected/expired or outside authorized zones.

Admin checklist and bootstrap

No public admin registration. Authorized invitation specifies role and descendant scope; candidate completes identity/KYC, secure credential setup and TOTP before activation. Sensitive roles receive additional checks. Initial Super Admin bootstrap is an offline two-person ceremony with unique accounts, recovery custody and documented emergency access—not a shared hardcoded password.

Enrollment flow: identity challenge → authenticator QR/secret shown once over secure session → verify current TOTP → issue single-use recovery codes once → activate account → security notification. Store TOTP secrets only in the identity provider's protected credential store. Test Google Authenticator-compatible time-step/algorithm settings against the selected pinned provider version; a feature list is not an interoperability test.

Every privileged login requires password + TOTP. New/suspicious device triggers additional email verification; the final master's risk-based policy supersedes the earlier suggestion to email a code on every login. Step-up is repeated for scope grants, KYC approval, payout/refund approval, destination changes, exports and emergency actions. Recovery requires identity proof, single-use code consumption, notification and session review; support cannot read or reuse recovery codes. Lost-device recovery must not silently remove MFA.

Access, retention and test gates

  • KYC bucket denies anonymous access and search indexing. Signed access is reviewer/object/purpose-specific, proposed 60-second TTL; prefer a no-store proxy when supported.
  • Logs contain case/document IDs, not full NID/passport/bank numbers. Review UI watermarks identify session/scope; browser capture prevention is not promised.
  • Proposed retention targets pending owner/legal approval: rejected/unneeded uploads shortest feasible; raw verification evidence only as required; financial records according to applicable law; deletion jobs verify object and derivative removal. Do not invent a statutory period from the historical chat.
  • Test unauthorized reviewer, cross-scope admin, expired URL, public object access, malicious upload, duplicate callback/upload, self-approval, expired document, renewal, lost authenticator, office-assisted consent and emergency revocation.

Official identity-provider documentation describes TOTP enrollment and account-linking flows; automatic linking to a same-email local account is explicitly a security risk. Disable unsafe email-only linking and require authenticated proof-based linking. 1 4

Brand and responsive rules

Retain the supplied Get Stoopy shopping-bag G logo, wordmark and “Shop Smart. Live Better.” identity. Recreate approved composition with semantic responsive components, not one stretched screenshot. Obtain original vector logo/photography rights before production; do not invent trademark registration from the ™ symbol.

  • Proposed tokens, to verify against original brand assets: brand.primary #B30D1B, hover #8F0A15, ink #15171A, surface #FFFFFF, muted #F5F6F8, border #E2E5E9, champagne #C6A56B. These are implementation proposals, not measured exact screenshot colors. Test contrast; use dark red for small text/links where needed.
  • Centralized typography/spacing/radius/shadow/focus tokens; shared buttons, forms, tables, cards, dialogs, toasts, skeletons, empty/error states and chart components. Use shadcn/ui accessibility primitives; Bengali font coverage and English/Bengali line heights tested.
  • Desktop reference layout; tablet reflow; mobile drawer/bottom navigation where appropriate, stacked cards, horizontally scrollable tables with labels, sticky primary action only when it does not obscure content. Keyboard focus, labels, errors, reduced motion, screen-reader chart summaries and touch targets are acceptance requirements.
  • Restrained chart/hero transitions only; no heavy animation. Recharts is a candidate retained from history; exact dependency/version selected in Phase 2. Product images require alt text and explicit dimensions.

DESIGN DOCUMENT · 09-source-review.md

Source review, coverage and limitations

Review date: 2026-11-01. This document distinguishes user decisions, historical proposals, visual fixtures and verified external facts.

Workspace inspection

No Git repository, application source, database, migration, environment file, dependency lockfile or deployment was present. Five uploaded reference images were available and visually inspected. Nothing existing was overwritten. The workspace now contains documentation, logical contracts, diagram sources/renders and documentation-generation/validation scripts only.

Shared conversation recovery

Source: https://chatgpt.com/share/6ae70089-14c4-83ec-aaf9-b382b6b04347

The ordinary page fetch exposed only the application shell. The public HTML's embedded serialized response was decoded locally without executing remote scripts. The recovered graph contained 633 nodes, from which 460 visible messages were retained: 209 user messages in 203 grouped turns and 251 assistant replies. User audio transcriptions were recovered where present. Other graph nodes are structural/metadata entries and are not claimed as additional readable messages.

Persisted evidence:

File Coverage
../research/visible-conversation.json 460 visible messages with source indexes/roles/transcriptions
../research/conversation-transcript.md Full retained visible transcript
../research/user-requirements-transcript.md All 209 user messages / 203 groups; fully reviewed
../research/historical-business-proposals.md Focused business/finance/geography extracts; fully reviewed
../research/historical-ai-and-admin.md Focused AI/admin/privacy extracts; fully reviewed
../research/historical-security-and-design.md Focused security/design extracts; fully reviewed
../research/other-assistant-replies.md Remaining 224 assistant replies; fully reviewed
../research/conversation-attachments.json Six historical image pointers and dimensions
../contracts/source-manifest.json Six current upload hashes/dimensions and conversation counts
../contracts/requirements-register.csv Atomic source-line requirements, historical additions and screenshot inventory

Focused extracts overlap the full transcript; they are not additional messages. All 251 retained assistant replies were reviewed across focused extracts plus the remaining-reply file. An assistant proposal is not automatically a user-approved requirement.

What could not be recovered

  • Private/internal reasoning, redacted code/tool output and unavailable historical image binaries were not accessible and were not invented.
  • Six historical image pointers are not proof that they are byte-identical to the five current uploads; no such identity is asserted.
  • The original master-script attachment/message was not independently archived in the recovered share transcript. 00-master-instructions.md is a normalized reconstruction from the supplied task context, checked against the retained requirements. It is not certified byte-for-byte identical to an original file. The final Bengali instruction is retained; uncertain wording is not silently corrected.
  • No original production logo/vector asset or photography license was supplied. The screenshot logo is a visual reference, not a verified trademark/license asset.

Precedence and conflict handling

  1. Final master instructions and explicit later user corrections control.
  2. Approved current Get Stoopy visuals control brand/layout, but mock numbers/claims are not business facts.
  3. Earlier user requests remain in traceability; where superseded, the conflict and resolution are recorded.
  4. Assistant-generated suggestions are proposals unless accepted by the user.
  5. Provider capability/legal claims require authoritative current evidence and merchant-specific confirmation.
Conflict Resolution retained
Green theme suggestions vs final red/white/black Final red accents, ordinary white backgrounds, dark navigation/footer; no green brand replacement
Buyer GPS must match destination vs remote gifting Separate buyer/recipient; recipient destination controls service; buyer location only risk evidence
Immediate wallet withdrawal / twice-weekly / manual-only vs final Sunday Sunday automatic payout default plus manual/verified bank option; exact cutoff pending
Rider travel/traffic/waiting bonus suggestions Rejected; fixed store→recipient road-distance slabs, admin-configured
Automatic ready after prep timer Rejected; vendor manually confirms ready
Every-login Gmail code vs final master Mandatory privileged TOTP; risk-based new/suspicious-device email challenge
Separate AI microservice vs modular monolith AI module/worker initially; extraction only after measured need
Apple in login image vs Google/Facebook/LinkedIn/X in master Apple optional inventoried addition; specified providers remain required when configured
Worldwide/free shipping/payment logos Capability- and policy-driven display; not enabled by a mockup
Admin chart $48,750 vs bars totaling $119,000 Mock inconsistency; real aggregates must reconcile
Vendor “Last 30 Days” with seven weekday labels Use period-consistent dates/buckets in implementation
Historical legal/QR assertions Not treated as verified law or acquirer permission

External research boundary

Official documentation was consulted for identity, routing, ORM and payment entry points. Search snippets are not a substitute for a provider contract. SSLCOMMERZ's reviewed public v4 page is dated 2019; aamarPay documents signed IPN and transaction lookup; shurjoPay capabilities remain to be confirmed from current merchant documentation. Keycloak account-linking and TOTP features require configuration/interoperability tests. Google Routes exposes road distance/duration and matrix operations; pricing/coverage/quotas remain deployment decisions. Prisma 8's PostGIS extension was announced in October 2026; exact release maturity and pinned compatibility must be verified before implementation. 1 2 1 2

No paid service, merchant account, OAuth app, cloud resource or production deployment was created. No legal opinion is offered.

Traceability method and honest limit

The generator retains every non-heading, non-note line of the normalized master, including standalone prose and list items, with source line references. Headings supply section/phase context. Historical additions and every inventory row from the six images are added separately. This provides broad, auditable coverage of the available text, not a proof that every unavailable artifact or ambiguous human intention has been recovered. Acceptance IDs are planned mappings, not passed tests.

DESIGN DOCUMENT · 10-payment-integrations.md

Payment, QR, payout and integration readiness

Status: research and secure interface design only. No merchant account, credential, payment, subscription, cloud resource or live integration exists.

Non-negotiable capability gate

A payment gateway accepting customer payments does not automatically authorize marketplace fund custody, split settlement, rider payouts or vendor disbursement. Obtain the legal entity, acquirer agreement, permitted flow, settlement account ownership, refund/dispute rules, fees, limits, API documentation and sandbox access before enabling any live capability. Never infer eligibility from a logo or an old chat response.

Capability Required evidence before live flag Current state
SSLCOMMERZ customer checkout Merchant approval, supported methods, exact validation/refund contract Adapter designed; not connected
aamarPay customer checkout Merchant approval, signed IPN specification, lookup/refund rules Adapter designed; not connected
shurjoPay customer checkout Merchant approval, token/verification/refund API contract Adapter designed; not connected
Central Bangla QR Acquirer-approved marketplace merchant flow, dynamic order QR, reconciliation, refund/dispute terms Disabled; unverified
MFS rider payout Approved disbursement product, beneficiary verification, limits/fees, callback/reconciliation Disabled; unverified
Bank payout/settlement Bank contract, file/API format, maker–checker, returns/reversals, statement import Disabled; unverified
Vendor direct QR/acquiring Contract identifying actual payee and settlement path Disabled; ledger reconciliation required
Google/Facebook/LinkedIn/X OAuth Approved apps, exact redirect URIs, scopes, provider-specific verification Not provisioned
Apple OAuth (visual reference) Owner approval + Apple app configuration Optional; not required by master
Google Routes/Matrix Approved billing project, restricted key, quotas/cost budget, BD route coverage test Candidate; not provisioned
Email/SMS/push/WhatsApp Approved sender/account, consent/templates, opt-out and cost policy Not provisioned
AI model provider Data-processing terms, retention policy, budget, scoped tool evaluation Not provisioned

Adapter contract

Each adapter declares capabilities rather than pretending every provider supports every operation: createCheckout, verifyTransaction, parseCallback, queryStatus, refund, queryRefund, dynamicOrderQR, disburse, verifyBeneficiary, reconcileStatement. Unsupported operations return a typed capability error and keep the feature disabled.

Server stores provider account, country, merchant reference, encrypted credentials, environment, contract reference and capability version. Checkout creates a unique merchant transaction reference and exact amount/currency before redirect. Callback handler verifies provider authenticity, persists a redacted event, deduplicates, queries/validates provider status and compares merchant/order/amount/currency. Only then posts payment verification and outbox events. Browser return page only displays current server state.

Provider event IDs may be absent: derive a stable dedupe key only after understanding provider semantics; transaction status transitions must not collapse distinct refunds/disputes. Store event hash and provider reference; do not log raw secrets. Out-of-order callbacks cannot regress a verified payment/refund. Unknown results reconcile before retry. Network timeout is not failure or success.

Provider-specific research notes

SSLCOMMERZ: the public v4 documentation says to validate the transaction through the Order Validation API and match stored order, amount, currency and status; IPN/redirect alone is insufficient. It lists validation/query/refund entry points, but the public page reviewed is dated 2019. Current merchant API and refund permissions must be reconfirmed. High gateway risk calls for holding service and verifying the customer. 2

aamarPay: official documentation advertises signed webhook notifications for successfully completed payments and a Search Transaction Details API for additional verification. Obtain the actual signature algorithm, replay window and current sandbox/live endpoints from the merchant contract; do not invent a common HMAC format. Signed-notification support is documented, but split settlement/dynamic QR/payout eligibility is not established. 2

shurjoPay: official onboarding/developer entry points remain the source for credentials and verification/refund behavior. Public third-party plugin examples are not authoritative evidence of current production API or security. Use TLS verification, short-lived token handling, provider verification and merchant-specific documentation. No claim that a refund or payout API is available until confirmed. Official entry: https://www.shurjopay.com.bd/frontend-developers/frontend-developers-page

Do not copy public sandbox credentials into the repository. Even shared test credentials belong in approved environment configuration; live credentials never appear in docs, screenshots, frontend bundles or source control.

Bangla QR decision

Preferred historical flow: customer scans a central marketplace order QR; verified payment maps to the exact parent order; backend splits/accounting handles vendor/rider obligations only if the approved merchant structure permits it. QR payload must be server-generated for amount/order/expiry where supported. A static personal QR or uploaded screenshot is not proof of payment.

If central collection is not permitted, present an owner-approved alternative: direct vendor acquiring with explicit payee disclosure and separate platform invoicing/reconciliation, or disable QR. Do not silently route customer money through a rider/personal account. Dynamic QR, instant merchant settlement, refund and dispute capabilities require acquirer confirmation. News about a 2026 QR directive was found, but no authoritative circular was verified; it is not used as legal authority.

Payout and settlement readiness

Rider Sunday automatic payout is the requested business default, not proof of a supported bank rail. If no verified destination or disbursement contract exists, show PAYOUT_BLOCKED with reason; preserve earned balance, do not fabricate transfer success. Manual withdrawal and verified bank option use the same financial controls. Provider-specific batch cutoff, holidays, fees, beneficiary names and reversal handling must be documented before activation.

Vendor settlement remains separately configurable and initially maker–checker approved. Reconcile gateway settlement, COD deposits, commission, refunds and bank statements daily. A provider's acceptance of a refund request is not completed refund; track until verified. Preserve chargeback evidence and immutable ledger adjustments.

Sandbox and live acceptance gates

  1. Contract/capability checklist signed by owner and provider; no assumed split/QR/payout support.
  2. Sandbox credentials supplied securely; test data labelled TEST_ONLY; no real money.
  3. Test success/failure/cancel, tampered amount/currency/order, invalid signature, replay, duplicate/out-of-order callback, timeout/unknown, partial/full refund, chargeback and reconciliation.
  4. Demonstrate idempotent payout reservation/execution and verified destination change cooldown.
  5. Independent security review and owner authorization before live credentials; separate explicit production deployment approval.

No payment screenshot, sample dashboard amount or generated UI state can satisfy these gates.

DESIGN DOCUMENT · 11-ai-and-personalization.md

AI, personalization, communication and optional feature scope

Status: retained requirements and proposed safeguards; no AI provider, tracking, microphone access or messaging integration is enabled.

First-party personalization

Collect only consented first-party events: product views, searches, wishlist/cart actions, purchases, explicit category interests and feedback. Guest personalization uses a first-party identifier with clear controls; authenticated cross-device sync is opt-in. Provide “Why am I seeing this?”, interest management, frequency limits, exclude category, clear history, opt out and delete/export propagation. No prechecked consent. With consent withdrawn, stop new collection and invalidate derived profiles/caches.

Homepage sections can include recently viewed, related products, saved-item price/stock alerts, reorder suggestions, trending in the selected service area and personalized deals. Cold-start uses non-personalized popular/new items. Filter by destination availability, stock, age/category policy and budget; never recommend an unavailable cross-border product as deliverable. Vendor reports use aggregates with privacy thresholds, not raw customer browsing histories.

Historical device-local interest inference is retained only as a consented, explainable first-party feature. Do not claim to read other apps, private messages, calls or ambient audio. Voice search starts only after a visible user action and browser permission; show recording state, transcript/edit/stop/delete controls and send only the intended query to the configured provider. Product sharing uses explicit share-sheet/copy-link action; it does not grant access to Facebook/WhatsApp/IMO/Viber/X conversations.

Role-specific assistants

Role Allowed assistance Sensitive boundary
Customer Natural-language product search, filters/comparison, product Q&A grounded in catalog, complaint intake, own order status, reorder suggestions No hidden purchases, price changes or access to another order
Vendor Draft descriptions/alt text, image suggestions, inventory/low-stock alerts, demand/sales forecast, pricing recommendations, performance summary Human publishes/changes price; no payout/refund/KYC execution
Rider Road navigation, voice guidance, delivery priority, own earnings explanation, approved customer communication templates, SOS workflow No covert recording, arbitrary location sharing or assignment override
Local/City/Regional/Country Admin Scoped operational summaries, anomaly alerts, vendor/rider performance, compliance reminders, forecast/report drafts Same scope as underlying data; no global cache/report leakage
Super Admin Global summaries, fraud/compliance investigation assistance, policy/campaign drafts Still cannot bypass maker–checker, ledger immutability or role-grant controls

AI service initially lives inside the modular monolith as an application module plus worker jobs. The earlier separate AI microservice proposal is superseded by the master's modular-monolith requirement. Extract later only for measured isolation/scale need.

Tool and approval design

Agent has its own workload identity. Effective scope = caller grants ∩ agent grants ∩ country/feature policy. Tools are typed, allowlisted, read-only by default, timeout/budget-limited and grounded in scoped services. Retrieved product descriptions, tickets and documents are untrusted data, not instructions. Redact PII before model calls where possible; provider retention/training terms require approval. Log prompt/output hashes, minimized summaries, tool calls, denials, cost and model version.

Prohibited tools: transfer/payout, refund approval, KYC approval, role/scope grant, ledger edit/delete, payment destination change. AI may create a draft proposal with exact payload hash. A human with normal permission reviews and approves through the domain command, with step-up/maker–checker where required. Approval expires and cannot be reused for a changed payload. No “approve all future actions” shortcut.

Notifications and safety

Email, SMS, in-app and push adapters are planned; WhatsApp is outbound only through an approved business API and consent/template policy. Separate service/security messages from marketing preferences. No private-chat ingestion. Notification content minimizes recipient/KYC data and locks sensitive details behind authentication.

Rider SOS is an explicit button with confirmation where safe, current consented location, emergency contact/support routing and audit. It does not imply automatic police/ambulance dispatch or continuous off-shift tracking. Show actual available response channel; no fabricated “help is on the way.”

Optional historical features retained

  • Loyalty points, cashback, referrals and membership tiers: feature-flagged, append-only award/reversal/expiry, anti-abuse and financial liability accounting.
  • Verified reviews, product comparison, vendor reliability indicators, transparent pricing and dispute/refund tracking.
  • Bengali/English first; locale/country-configurable additional languages. Currency display does not imply multicurrency settlement.
  • Vendor Free/Basic/Plus/Pro plans, first-year free introductory offer, volume limits and renewal history; exact commercial terms pending approval.
  • Manual/hybrid courier adapter, batching/multi-pickup optimization and native mobile wrapper: later flags, not silently enabled.
  • PWA install/offline shell and explicit foreground location; browser background GPS is unreliable. Native capture restrictions require a supported native app and still cannot stop another camera.

Evaluation gates

Test consent withdrawal/deletion, guest→login merge, cross-scope retrieval, unavailable-product recommendations, prompt injection, prohibited tool denial, exact-action approval, hallucinated order/payment status, budget limits and provider outage. Measure recommendation relevance and assistant groundedness without claiming perfect predictions. Ordinary catalog/checkout must work with AI disabled.

Required-name mapping

Master name Physical design
VendorLedger LedgerAccount(ownerType=VENDOR) + LedgerLine view
RiderLedger LedgerAccount(ownerType=RIDER, purpose=EARNINGS/RESERVE) + LedgerLine view
CODLedger LedgerAccount(ownerType=RIDER, purpose=COD_CUSTODY) + CODCollection/Deposit/Allocation
RiderLocation Active-shift/active-delivery records with restrictive retention
VendorKYC / RiderKYC Role-specific extension of KYCCase; AdminKYC also included

Index / constraint implementation plan

  • B-tree: every concrete FK; status/time composites for orders, offers, KYC, payouts and audit; public references and provider transaction keys unique.
  • GiST: BoundaryVersion.boundary, Address.point, Store.pickupPoint, RiderLocation.point; rider/time and shift/time B-tree companions.
  • Partial unique: one open shift per rider; one active assignment per delivery; one active offer per delivery; active provider references where present.
  • Deferred constraint triggers: balanced journal lines and matching currency; inventory nonnegative/reserved bounds; allocation caps; ancestry checks where composite FKs cannot express them.
  • Polymorphic ownerId/subjectId/resourceId/aggregateId/referenceId are logical references, not fake foreign keys. Validate type+ID in guarded commands; use concrete join tables where integrity requires it.
  • Circular current-case/address/boundary pointers are nullable and validated/deferred. Immutable history remains the authority; never delete history to change a pointer.
  • UUID targetKey=id unless explicitly documented. Relationship cardinality is FK-owner→target; optional means nullable. Business cardinality such as one current delivery is a separate partial constraint.

Retention proposal — owner/legal approval required

Data class Proposed operational target Deletion / hold rule
Active account/profile While active + closure processing Delete/minimize on verified request unless lawful hold
KYC uploads and raw identity evidence Shortest policy-required period; rejected/unneeded evidence promptly purged Legal/contractual schedule must be approved before collection
Raw rider GPS ≤30 days after collection Keep only required route/dispute evidence; no off-shift stream
First-party personalization events ≤180 days Clear derived profiles/caches on opt-out/delete
Session/security metadata ≤90 days after expiry/revocation unless incident hold Hash tokens; restrict access
Orders/recipient snapshots Business support window then minimize Financial/tax hold only for required fields
Financial journals/payout evidence Applicable statutory/contractual period Immutable; never reset by deleting transactions
Audit logs ≥12 months proposed; sensitive access longer if approved Tamper-evident restricted archive; legal hold
Backups Encrypted rolling window proposed ≤35 days Expiry plus documented deletion propagation on restore
Support/SOS evidence Purpose-specific shortest window Restricted access; incident/legal hold documented
No period above is a claim about Bangladesh law. Counsel/provider review must set the final retention register before real data collection.

BN-310-001 00-master-instructions.md:L1175; section Bengali addendum আচ্ছা স্ক্রিনশটে এর ফিচারগুলা এড করা নেই, এই জিনিসটারে তুমি এড করে দিবে যে যে ফিচারগুলো উল্লেখ করা আছে, একটা ইনফরমেশনও যেন মিছ আউট না হয় তাহলে কিন্তু অনেক বড় লস হয়ে যাবে, তুমি প্রত্যেকটা ইনফরমেশন রিট করে এবং তোমাকে আমার চ্যাট ডিভিডির কনভারসেশনও দিয়েছি সেগুলো ফলো করবে এবং স্ক্রিপ্টটা দিয়েছি সেটাও ফলো করবে ইনফরমেশনও যেন মিস না যায়। আর সিকিউরিটির বিষয়টা তো সব সময় মাথায় রাখতে হবে তোমার আর কন্টাকনোলজি দিয়ে করবে সেটাও বলা আছে। All phases 00-master-instructions.md Source instruction

DESIGN DOCUMENT · 14-roadmap.md

Development roadmap and acceptance gates

Status: Phase 1 review package prepared; Phase 1 approval pending. Phases 2–11 not started. No application acceptance test has run because no application exists.

Execution rules

Follow the master order. Security, schema constraints, audit, accessibility and tests are introduced with each feature, not postponed to a final “security phase.” A phase may have a reviewable vertical slice before later integrations, but cannot be marked complete until its acceptance gates pass. Missing external credentials produce disabled adapters and documented blockers, never fake live behavior. No production deployment without separate explicit authorization.

Phase Deliverables Exit gate / evidence Current status
1 — Discovery & architecture Source review; normalized master; architecture; logical ERD/dictionary; RBAC/geography; OpenAPI; threat model; finance/KYC/provider policies; roadmap/ADRs Owner reviews critical decisions and unresolved gates; document/model/contract validation passes; no implementation implied Prepared — awaiting review
2 — Foundation Monorepo; pinned dependencies; design tokens; Docker/CI; PostgreSQL/PostGIS migrations; identity/session/MFA; RBAC/ABAC/RLS; audit/outbox; private storage interface Migration/rollback and constraint tests; auth/linking/MFA/recovery tests; cross-scope negative tests; accessible shell; CI green Not started
3 — Customer website Approved homepage; locale; catalog/search/categories/products; cart/wishlist; recipient-first quote/checkout; account/orders/tracking/returns/support Responsive visual comparison; real DB catalog; remote-order and stock/price tests; no unsupported claims; payment sandbox only when approved Not started
4 — Vendor Application/KYC; stores/staff; products/variants/images/stock; accept/reject/prep/manual ready; returns; commission/settlement views; plans Vendor isolation; KYC/expiry gates; manual-ready test; multi-vendor split; settlement view reconciles; no cross-store leakage Not started
5 — Rider KYC/vehicle; shift/consent/location; zones; road-distance offers; 30-second expiry; atomic assignment; pickup/OTP; earnings/COD; Sunday payout interface Concurrent/expired offer tests; route/rate snapshots; OTP limits; independent COD/earnings; payout reserve/idempotency; mobile/PWA limits documented Not started
6 — Admin systems Super/Country/Regional/City/Zone/Local shells; KYC/finance/fraud/geography/security/operations; reports/exports; AI-safe approval surfaces Every role/scope negative test; no self-scope grant; maker–checker; export/read audit; scoped aggregates/sockets; emergency lock drill Not started
7 — Payments & finance Provider adapters; verified callbacks; COD reconciliation; commission/refund/chargeback; vendor settlement; rider payout reconciliation; QR only if approved Sandbox callback/tamper/replay/refund tests; balanced journals; provider/bank reconciliation; verified destinations; no duplicate money effects; live remains off Not started
8 — Security & fraud Harden MFA/KYC/session controls; risk engine/manual review; audit monitoring; upload/export defenses; independent review Threat-model test coverage; security scans/review; revocation/restore/alert drills; risk acceptance for residual issues Not started
9 — AI Consented personalization; search/shopping assistance; vendor drafts/forecasts; rider guidance; scoped admin summaries; human approvals Consent/delete tests; groundedness/evaluation set; prompt-injection/tool-denial tests; budgets; core works with AI off Not started
10 — QA Unit/integration/E2E/API/security/accessibility/performance; realistic pilot load; failure/recovery tests All required acceptance scenarios pass; defects triaged; measured budgets; no disabled security to pass; evidence linked to requirements Not started
11 — Deployment preparation Env template; Docker/CI; deployment/backup/runbooks; user guides; monitoring/WAF; production checklist; handover Staging rehearsal and restore drill; contracts/credentials/security/legal gates documented; owner authorizes production separately Not started

Critical path

Approved architecture → foundation/auth/scope → catalog + recipient checkout → vendor split/ready → rider assignment/OTP → immutable earnings/COD → verified payment/payout adapters → scoped admin operations → security/fraud hardening → AI → full QA → deployment rehearsal

Finance invariants and permission tests begin in Phase 2. Earlier phases may use explicitly labelled test adapters; they cannot claim a real provider integration. The first end-to-end vertical slice should cover a remote gift, two vendors, one rider per suborder, recipient OTP, COD custody and immutable earnings before optional loyalty/AI expansion.

Final acceptance mapping

ID Required outcome Planned evidence
ACC-F01 Register/login/browse/search/order API + Playwright customer flows, verification/session tests
ACC-F02 Multi-vendor parent/suborder split DB transaction and vendor-isolation tests
ACC-F03 Vendor accept/prepare/manual ready State-machine/API/E2E tests; timer cannot auto-ready
ACC-F04 Eligible rider receives/completes delivery KYC/zone/shift/capacity and concurrent-offer tests
ACC-F05 Recipient OTP Rate-limit/replay/expiry/wrong-recipient tests
ACC-F06 Admin distance-slab earnings Boundary/effective-date/snapshot/invariance tests
ACC-F07 Independent COD/earnings reconciliation Journal, partial/duplicate deposit and allocation tests
ACC-F08 Sunday payout under verified conditions Asia/Dhaka schedule, destination, reserve, retry/unknown-result tests
ACC-F09 Vendor commission/settlement Default exclusion of delivery, rounding, partial refund and double-settlement tests
ACC-F10 KYC review/authorization Document access, self-approval denial, expiry/renewal tests
ACC-F11 Admin TOTP Enrollment/login/recovery/step-up/revocation tests
ACC-F12 API geographic isolation SQL/API/report/export/cache/socket negative tests
ACC-F13 Remote ordering Different buyer/recipient location positive test; destination controls
ACC-F14 Fraud review/audit Hold/review/appeal and sensitive-read/write audit tests
ACC-F15 Verified/idempotent callbacks Provider-specific authenticity, server validation, replay/tamper tests
ACC-F16 Approved responsive brand Desktop/tablet/mobile visual review and accessibility tests
ACC-F17 Automated tests pass CI report linked to exact commit; no application report exists yet
ACC-F18 Production requirements documented Runbooks/checklist/restore evidence; deployment still separately approved

Deferred by explicit gate, not forgotten

Cross-border checkout, US activation, live payments, central Bangla QR, real disbursement, native wrapper, batching, courier hybrid, loyalty/cashback/referrals and paid AI/maps/notification services remain disabled until their commercial/legal/security prerequisites are satisfied. First-year vendor relief and configurable plans remain in the model; exact prices/volume terms need owner approval.

Estimate policy

No calendar-day promise is made before repository/provider decisions and pilot load are approved. After Phase 1 approval, estimate each phase from reviewed tasks and update progress with actual evidence. A large feature list is not a reason to skip tests or silently reduce scope.

No running marketplace backend, live integration, paid resource or production deployment exists. See 17-phase2-foundation.md.

Proposed choices needing architecture review

ID Proposal Alternative / consequence
D01 Next.js BFF + NestJS modular monolith + worker Well-structured Next backend is permitted; Nest adds explicit domain/guard structure and another deployable
D02 Keycloak identity + opaque revocable BFF sessions Maintained database-session auth framework if owner rejects identity-service operations; no JWT-only shortcut
D03 PostgreSQL/PostGIS + Prisma with reviewed spatial adapter Pin a compatible release after Phase-2 compatibility spike; Prisma 8 extension is new, not assumed production-proven
D04 Google Routes/Matrix candidate Another road-routing provider can be selected; no straight-line substitute for required road pay/dispatch
D05 Private S3-compatible storage + KMS Managed equivalent acceptable after access/retention/encryption review
D06 Double-entry immutable journals; role ledger views Avoids competing mutable wallets; requires deferred balance constraints and reconciliation
D07 Earnings route/rate snapshot at final acceptance Offer-time snapshot is an explicit business alternative; no retroactive changes either way
D08 Destination-scoped local operations; separate financial-scope anchor Owner must approve cross-zone report visibility and vendor finance anchor
D09 Mobile-first PWA initially Native wrapper later for supported background/capture controls; honest browser limitations
D10 White/black/red tokens and approved layout Exact brand asset/color confirmation at visual review; no green theme

Business/provider information still needed

  1. Approve architecture and identity operating model; provide original repository if one exists outside this workspace.
  2. Confirm legal merchant entity, verified contact details, logo/vector rights and actual support hours/policies.
  3. Confirm pilot polygons, launch stores, operating hours, delivery/customer fee policy and funded free-delivery campaigns.
  4. Set rider distance slabs/min/max, commission defaults/overrides, Sunday cutoff/holiday policy, payout fees/minimum and any disclosed COD offset.
  5. Confirm vendor settlement hold/eligibility, first-year-free scope, plan prices/volume limits and renewal consent.
  6. Approve KYC document/retention policy with qualified local review; identify only authorized verification channels.
  7. Provide provider contracts/sandbox access when ready: payments, QR, MFS/bank payout, OAuth, maps, email/SMS/push/WhatsApp and AI. Missing items remain disabled.
  8. Choose cloud/residency/budget/domain/on-call owner before any paid provisioning; production authorization remains separate.

None of these blockers justifies fabricated credentials, payments, KYC results or production data. Development can proceed with secure interfaces and clearly labelled test fixtures after architecture approval, within the approved no-paid-resource boundary.

Local development boundary

Copy .env.example to .env and replace local-only placeholders before starting containers. Do not commit .env. The compose file binds services to localhost for development; it is not a production deployment. Keycloak realm template disables public registration and implicit/direct-grant flows and configures TOTP policy, but the privileged-admin mandatory MFA flow, Argon2id selection and safe linking still require implementation/testing.
